suggested_requirements.text: The HATS-GUI shall provide the user with the ability to construct and use transformations.
The HATS-GUI shall facilitate the creation, deletion, and modification of the files related to an application.
The HATS-GUI shall manage file associations within an application.
The HATS-GUI shall allow the user to examine and modify file associations.
The HATS-GUI shall orchestrate the parsing of transformation language programs and target files.
The HATS-GUI shall orchestrate the execution of transformation language programs.
The HATS-GUI shall capture data written to debugging and error streams and make that data available to the user.
The HATS-GUI shall facilitate the display of transformation output and error messages received from HATS-SML.
The HATS-GUI shall make a list of files available to the user and allow the user to select files for display.
The HATS-GUI shall allow the user to manipulate the display by choosing portions of the tree to display and by allowing the user to search for text strings and sub-trees.

The HATS-GUI shall allow a user to create an application minimally consisting of a lexical specification file, a grammar file, a user-defined functions file, and application configuration information.
The HATS-GUI shall allow the user to specify the number of levels of nodes to expand during SDT viewing.
The HATS-GUI shall allow the user to select the colors for types of displayed nodes in a displayed graph.
The HATS-GUI shall allow the user to select the shapes for types of displayed nodes in a displayed graph.

The HATS-GUI shall interface with HATS-SML (version 2.0) in order to parse transformation language programs, execute transformation language programs, and create output SDTs, error messages, pretty-printed text, and parsed transformation language programs.
The HATS-GUI shall allow the user to create, modify, copy, or delete applications or files regardless of the current status of HATS-SML.
The HATS-GUI shall interact with the HOST OS file services to create, delete, open, read, write, and close files.
The HATS-GUI shall interact with the HOST OS to find files in directories.
The HATS-GUI shall interact with the HOST OS to compare time stamps for files.
The HATS-GUI shall prompt the user to confirm deletion prior to completing file or application deletion.
The system shall be completed by December 2001.
The system shall be platform independent and function properly on any operating system, specifically Sun Solaris, Windows 2000, and Linux.
The system shall be designed in such a way as to minimize the number of windows opened by the application.
The system shall be developed using the Java programming language.
The HATS-GUI shall be menu driven.
All files associated with a given application shall be stored in one directory.
